In [[mathematics]], the '''reflexive closure''' of a [[binary relation]] <math>R</math> on a [[Set (mathematics)|set]] <math>X</math> is the smallest [[reflexive relation]] on <math>X</math> that contains <math>R</math>, i.e. the set <math>R \cup \{(x,x) \mid x \in X  \}</math>.

For example, if <math>X</math> is a set of distinct numbers and <math>x R y</math> means "<math>x</math> is less than <math>y</math>", then the reflexive closure of <math>R</math> is the relation "<math>x</math> is less than or equal {{nowrap|to <math>y</math>".}}

==Definition==

The reflexive closure <math>S</math> of a relation <math>R</math> on a set <math>X</math> is given by
<math display=block>S = R \cup \{(x, x) \mid x \in X\}</math>

In plain English, the reflexive closure of <math>R</math> is the union of <math>R</math> with the [[identity relation]] on <math>X.</math>

==Example==

As an example, if
<math display=block>X = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}</math>
<math display=block>R = \{(1,1), (1,3), (2,2), (3,3), (4,4)\}</math>
then the relation <math>R</math> is already reflexive by itself, so it does not differ from its reflexive closure.

However, if any of the reflexive pairs in <math>R</math> was absent, it would be inserted for the reflexive closure.
For example, if on the same set <math>X</math>
<math display=block>R = \{(1,1), (1,3), (2,2), (4,4)\}</math>
then the reflexive closure is
<math display=block>S = R \cup \{(x,x) \mid x \in X\} = \{(1,1), (1,3), (2,2), (3,3), (4,4)\} .</math>
